elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: Inspection is by "HDI's General Manager"; no independent auditor or confidentiality obligation appears.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." (unconditional, more favourable to Customer)

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: Clause grants right "to inspect the records" but contains no express bar on access to Company systems.
"no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI" — cost sits on Vendor without any shift-back trigger

reasons: Locked target is fallback; all fallback atomic elements are met — annual frequency cap inserted, 30-day notice exceeds the 15-day minimum, and Vendor (HDI) bears inspection cost unconditionally, which is more favourable to Customer than the 10% carve-out.
Preferred level remains incomplete: no independent auditor bound by confidentiality and no express prohibition on direct access to Customer systems; these are noted, not required at the locked level.
Minimal: a single short insertion ("not more than once per year and") into the existing sentence; no rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate.
Intent preserved: notice period, business-hours limit, scope of records and cost allocation sentence remain untouched; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.
